clue.text: About whom PM needs to learn!

definitions.text: About whom PM needs to learn!

indicators.note: 'about' can mean round and round, so the letters that follow are turned about into a new order

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that the Prime Minister has some homework on a particular person.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: PETER MANDELSON, the Labour grandee and Prince of Darkness, is a figure any prime minister had to learn about. The fodder is every letter after 'About'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandelson was a famously influential Labour minister and adviser, the kind of figure a Labour premier must understand to survive politically.

clue.text: Doctors, supporting chest secured by rod, stop motor at this point

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another is written beneath it, so it comes after
something secured by a fastener is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a pin is a thin rod
an ark is a chest or coffer, as in the Ark of the Covenant
GP, a general practitioner, is an abbreviated doctor
to doctor a drink is to lace it

explanation.surface: Medics bracing a patient's chest with a rod, and somehow a car stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' works twice over, first as a noun for medics and then as a verb meaning to spike a drink, and both sit under the chest held in the rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A parking place is a space where a driver halts the car and leaves it, so it is where you stop your motor.

clue.text: Fade, Eeyore-style?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to dwindle away gradually
second meaning: Eeyore, the donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh, keeps losing his tail, which is pinned back on

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: Eeyore's tail is detachable and comes off in the stories, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail off is a phrasal verb for diminishing gradually until little remains, just as a sound or interest fades.

clue.text: I agree this is 7's city centre

indicators.note: only the centre is wanted, so the outermost letters at each end are dropped

parts.note: Laurence Olivier lived in this south-coast seaside city and took his life peerage as Baron Olivier of Brighton

explanation.surface: Someone nodding along that this is the downtown area of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7 refers to the answer at 7-down; once OLIVIER is in, his city is Brighton, and losing its first and last letters leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Righto is a chatty British interjection of assent, the same as saying okay or all right.

clue.text: Foreign lodger reported O2?

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters here, not the spelling

parts.note: O2 is a pair of Os, said as 'O pair'

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a foreign tenant connected with oxygen or the phone company.
explanation.walkthrough: O2 looks like oxygen or the London arena; read it as two Os, a pair of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young person from abroad who lives with a host family, helping with childcare in return for board.

clue.text: In musical gathering, sons and daughters exchange blows

definitions.note: a noun for a heated exchange of blows

indicators.note: each son gives way to a daughter, so one abbreviation swaps for another throughout

parts.note: a sing-song is an informal gathering where people sing together

explanation.surface: A family singalong where the children end up fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: S for son is replaced each time by D for daughter, both standard abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A ding-dong is British slang for a fierce argument or fight, a lively round of blows.

clue.text: Millie's Boy raised game, potting ball

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads from the bottom up
to pot is to put into a pocket, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: pool is the cue game played on a pocketed table
pill is an old slang word for a ball

explanation.surface: A singer's son lifts his game at the pool table by sinking a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Millie Small had a 1964 hit with 'My Boy Lollipop', so her boy is the answer. Potting a ball suits the pool surface perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title calls the singer's sweetheart her boy lollipop, so the name is what Millie's boy is called.

clue.text: Would it periodically rival The Entertainer?

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of these two words
a vier is one who vies, a competitor

explanation.surface: A question whether something could match a famous stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Entertainer, John Osborne's play and its 1960 film, starred Laurence Olivier as Archie Rice, so the title stands for its star.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivier played the faded music-hall performer Archie Rice in both the stage and screen versions, making him the original lead of that work.

clue.text: Regretful of downfall brought to leader of government

parts.note: ruin is a collapse or downfall

indicators.note: the leader goes in front of the rest, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sorry head of government contemplating a fall from power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of' picks the first letter; the definition includes 'of' because ruing takes an object, as regretful of does.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to feel sorrow over something, so someone ruing a mistake is sorry about it.

clue.text: Review endlessly of assistance to fixer

indicators.note: without ends at either side, so the first and last letters are lost

parts.note: to pan is to give something a harsh review
helping means being of assistance

explanation.surface: A critic's endless help offered to someone who fixes things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixer' suggests a person who sorts problems; here it is a thing that fixes, a small nail.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel pin is a slender nail with a small head used to fasten thin boards, so it fixes things together.

clue.text: Hit total … good number

parts.note: to come to a figure is to total it
G is the abbreviation for good
a number here is something that numbs, and ether is an old anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A tally of hits, with a good song among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a song or a figure but is read as numb-er, a thing that deadens feeling. Come Together is also a Beatles hit, which makes 'Hit' doubly fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that come together collide or meet, which is what hitting means; it is also a famous Beatles single.

clue.text: Invitation accepted: Odin, "timid" barking dog, bites postman's rear!

indicators.note: what bites something takes it into its mouth, so one letter goes inside
barking is British slang for mad, so these letters go wild and change order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its tail end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word
Fido is the stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: A god's timid dog that barks but still bites the postman, with an accepted invitation thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogs biting postmen is the comic picture; the reworked letters take in the N near their end, and the dog's name follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the polite stock reply when offered a drink or a treat, a way of saying yes, thank you.

clue.text: See 11
Rubbish flat, hooked stick
Going the right way towards the nineteenth hole?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: following the planned route
second meaning: the nineteenth hole is golfers' slang for the clubhouse bar, reached after playing a golf course

explanation.walkthrough: A golf round has eighteen holes; the nineteenth is the bar, and you head there while out on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: On course means proceeding as planned toward a goal, and literally describes a golfer still out playing.

clue.text: Stars — Miller, most frequently — breaking the heart of Marilyn Monroe

indicators.note: broken things come apart in pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letter that occurs most often in the name, appearing twice

indicators.note: the heart is the very middle, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arthur Miller, so often in the papers, breaking Marilyn Monroe's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Miller was Marilyn Monroe's husband, which makes the surface convincing. The L goes into the front of the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Minor, the Lesser Lion, is a small constellation in the northern sky, a group of stars.

clue.text: Heat Units look into degeneration of bones

indicators.note: to go into something is to enter it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: caries is decay of bone or teeth
lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: A medical team examining bone disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat Units' is capitalised to look like a hospital department or team name.
explanation.definitionFit: A calorie is a scientific unit of heat energy, the amount needed to warm a gram of water by one degree.

clue.text: Lima perhaps — very like, say, the world's entertainment capital

parts.note: Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet
as can mean perhaps, as in 'as it may be'
V is the abbreviation for very
e.g. introduces a thing like the one named
as means say, for instance

explanation.surface: Peru's capital, perhaps, likened to the world's capital of entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lima perhaps' looks like a capital city signalling a capital definition; Lima is just the letter. Every short word is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada city is famous for casinos and shows and calls itself the Entertainment Capital of the World.

clue.text: Bird Box 5

parts.note: to box is to spar
the answer at 5-down is a ding-dong, a quarrel, which is a row

explanation.surface: Bird Box looks like the title of a horror film or novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 refers to the answer at 5-down, which means a row; in Britain a row is a noisy quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird, one of the most familiar birds in gardens and cities.

clue.text: Too technical, some cases

indicators.note: the string of words acts as a case holding the letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A complaint that something has become too technical in some instances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too technical' reads as excessive jargon, but 'Too' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Too and also are synonyms meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: Rolling tract of country yours truly almost completely destroyed

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the order of letters is flipped
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a wold is an open stretch of upland country
the writer refers to themself as I
all means completely, as in 'all wrong'

explanation.surface: A writer describing their own rolling farmland laid waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' looks like a description of the landscape but is the reversal signal; the Wolds are English areas of rolling hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid low means brought down, ruined or crushed, as a defeated army or a sick person is.

clue.text: In which three Guineas pay for his coat in seconds

indicators.note: taking things in seconds means every second one, so alternate letters are kept

parts.note: the even letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Paying three guineas, an old British sum, for a coat in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: A guinea was an old British coin worth 21 shillings; here the Guineas are Guinea, Guinea-Bissau and Equatorial Guinea.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent contains three nations named Guinea, which is where the definition places them.

clue.text: Online handle attached to Louvre's principal work of art

parts.note: an e-name is an online username or handle

indicators.note: the principal one comes first in rank, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the gallery's name

explanation.surface: An internet username linked to the chief masterpiece of the Paris museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Online handle' reads as a username, and the e- prefix is the usual crossword shorthand for electronic.
explanation.definitionFit: An enamel is a decorative object made with fused glassy coating on metal, so an individual piece of art.

clue.text: Check marshy inlet — one's means to an end, very obligingly

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a campaign of flattery aimed at a goal

indicators.note: here the letter is added into the following piece, taken in to it

parts.note: ch is the chess abbreviation for check
an inlet is an arm, and one of a fen is marshy

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the one kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word
one has, from the speaker, is I've

explanation.surface: Checking a tidal creek in a marsh as a means to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one has', said by the speaker as I've. The S from the end of 'means' goes just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm offensive is a deliberate campaign of friendliness and flattery used to win people over to some purpose.

clue.text: See 23
Outside bishop is drinking Berlusconi's last toast to Renzi?

indicators.note: a drinker takes liquid inside, so one piece goes within others

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a rind is the outer skin of fruit or cheese
taken as written

indicators.note: last points at the final letter of the name before it

parts.note: the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: An outside bishop raising a glass to two Italian prime ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: Berlusconi and Matteo Renzi were Italian prime ministers, so the toast is an Italian one; brindisi is also a port city, which the definition avoids.
explanation.definitionFit: A brindisi is an Italian drinking song or toast, the kind sung to someone's health in opera.

clue.text: Soil enricher that additionally protects large cutting to a great extent

indicators.note: cutting into something splits it open and goes inside

parts.note: much means to a great degree
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A garden product that also shields a big cutting, a plant slip, very well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' reads as a gardener's plant cutting, which fits the soil picture, but it signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulch is a layer of compost or bark spread on soil to feed it and to protect roots and suppress weeds.

clue.text: Broadcaster's closing argument against Defence Act

indicators.note: to close round something is to shut it in, so pieces go inside

parts.note: a sower broadcasts seed by scattering it

indicators.note: against means up close beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: to have words is to argue
a wall is a defence around a property

explanation.surface: A TV presenter's summing-up opposing a parliamentary Defence Act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcaster' suggests radio or TV, but a farmer broadcasting seed is meant. 'Act' is a circus act, not legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword-swallower is a performer whose turn is sliding a blade down the throat, a classic sideshow or circus act.
